P.g: A. Code of Ethics
P.label: CoE: Fundamental principles
P.title: Fundamental principles (Subsections 111–115)
P.law: A professional accountant shall comply with five fundamental principles: Integrity, Objectivity, Professional competence and due care, Confidentiality and Professional behaviour.
notes: Integrity (111): straightforward and honest. Shall not knowingly be associated with reports/returns that contain materially false or misleading statements, statements provided negligently, or that omit/obscure required information. Not in breach if a modified report is issued. Once aware of such association, take steps to be disassociated.
Objectivity (112): do not compromise judgment because of bias, conflict of interest or undue influence; do not undertake an activity if a circumstance/relationship unduly influences judgment.

Professional competence and due care (113): attain and maintain knowledge and skill; act diligently per standards; CPD; ensure people under your authority are trained and supervised; tell users about inherent limitations of the service.
Confidentiality (114): see CoE: Confidentiality — disclosure. Continues after the relationship ends; prior experience may be used, confidential information may not.

Professional behaviour (115): comply with laws, avoid conduct that discredits the profession. When promoting yourself: no exaggerated claims, no disparaging references or unsubstantiated comparisons, no advertising in breach of Council's advertisement guidelines. In doubt about proposed advertising? Consult the Ethical Standards Board.
Conflict between principles: consult within firm, TCWG, legal counsel or the Institute; consultation does not relieve responsibility; document the issue, discussions, decisions and rationale.

Structure of Code: Part 1 (complying, principles, conceptual framework — all PAs), Part 2 (PAs in service), Part 3 (PAs in public practice), Part 4A (independence for audit and review), Part 4B (independence for other assurance), Glossary.
P.upd: Code of Ethics 2026 (13th edition) is in three volumes: Vol I = domestic provisions (CA Act, Schedules, Council guidelines), Vol II = converged with IESBA Code 2024 edition, Vol III = Ethics Standards for Sustainability Assurance (including independence). Applicable from 1 April 2026.

P.g: A. Code of Ethics
P.label: CoE: Threats & safeguards
P.title: Conceptual framework — threats, evaluation, safeguards
P.law: Identify threats → Evaluate them (acceptable level, reasonable and informed third party test) → Address them (eliminate the circumstance, apply safeguards, or decline/end the activity).
notes: Self-interest: financial interest in client; fee quoted so low the work can't be done to standard; close business relationship; access to confidential info usable for gain; discovering a significant error in a colleague's earlier work.
Self-review: assurance report on systems you implemented; you prepared the data that is the subject matter.
Advocacy: promoting client's shares; advocate for client in litigation; lobbying for client.
Familiarity: close/immediate family member is director/officer of client; ex-engagement partner now director of client; long association.
Intimidation: threat of dismissal over disagreement; pressure because client claims more expertise; promotion withheld unless you agree; threat to publicise a significant gift you accepted.

PA in service examples: incentive pay, loan from employer (self-interest); deciding accounting for a business combination after doing the feasibility study (self-review); manipulating a prospectus to get financing (advocacy); family member makes decisions affecting reporting (familiarity); dismissal threat over an accounting principle (intimidation).

Acceptable level: a level at which a reasonable and informed third party would likely conclude the PA complies with the principles. That third party need not be an accountant but has the knowledge to judge impartially.

Safeguards examples: extra time/qualified staff (self-interest); independent reviewer outside the team (self-review); separate partners/teams with separate reporting lines for non-assurance services (self-review, advocacy, familiarity); another firm re-performs part (all threats); separate teams for confidential matters (self-interest).
P.mem: SSAFI: Self-interest, Self-review, Advocacy, Familiarity, Intimidation.

P.g: A. Code of Ethics
P.label: CoE: Confidentiality — disclosure
P.title: Confidentiality — when disclosure is required or appropriate (Subsection 114)
P.short: when disclosure is required or appropriate (Subsection 114)
P.law: Disclose confidential information only with proper and specific authority, or where there is a legal or professional duty or right to disclose.
notes: (a) Required by law: production of documents/evidence in legal proceedings; disclosure to public authorities of infringements of law.
(b) Permitted by law and authorised by client/employer.

(c) Professional duty or right to disclose, when not prohibited by law: (i) Peer Review / Quality Review of the Institute; (ii) inquiry or investigation by a professional or regulatory body; (iii) to protect the PA's professional interests in legal proceedings; (iv) to comply with technical and professional standards, including ethics requirements.

Factors before disclosing: (1) could any party's interests, including third parties, be harmed even if the client consents; (2) is all relevant information known and substantiated; (3) the proposed type of communication and to whom; (4) are the recipients appropriate.
Be alert to inadvertent disclosure in a social setting, especially to close business associates and close/immediate family.
Link to the Act: practice → SS I(1); employee → SS II(2).

P.g: A. Code of Ethics
P.label: CoE: NOCLAR
P.title: Responding to Non-Compliance with Laws and Regulations (NOCLAR)
P.short: Responding to Non-Compliance with Laws and Regulations (NOCLAR)
P.law: NOCLAR = acts of omission or commission, intentional or unintentional, contrary to laws/regulations, committed by the client/employer, TCWG, management or others working for or under their direction.
notes: Not covered: personal misconduct unrelated to the business; non-compliance by parties outside the definition; clearly inconsequential matters.

Examples (IESBA): fraud, corruption, bribery; money laundering, terrorist financing, proceeds of crime; securities markets and trading; banking and financial products; data protection; tax and pension liabilities; environmental protection; public health and safety.

PA is not required to investigate, not responsible for ensuring compliance, and not expected to know law beyond what the engagement requires. Whether an act is non-compliance is ultimately for a court.

Applicability in India (per SM): PAs in service → Section 260: senior professional accountants (KMP: directors, officers, senior employees able to exert significant influence) employed in listed entities. PAs in practice → Section 360: audit engagements of entities whose shares are listed on recognised stock exchange(s) in India and net worth ≥ ₹250 crore. 'Audit' = reasonable assurance engagement expressing a true and fair opinion.

Steps: obtain an understanding → address the matter (discuss with management/TCWG) → seek advice → determine whether further action is needed → determine whether to disclose to an appropriate authority → imminent breach → documentation.

Imminent breach: if a breach would cause substantial harm to investors, creditors, employees or the public, after considering whether to discuss with management/TCWG, the PA may disclose immediately to an appropriate authority; such disclosure is permitted. Appropriate authority depends on the matter (e.g., SEBI for fraudulent financial reporting).
Extra documentation: how management/TCWG responded; actions considered, judgments and decisions (third party test); how the PA is satisfied the public-interest responsibility is fulfilled.

NOCLAR vs SA 250: (1) SA 250 applies only to audits; NOCLAR to PAs in service and in practice, including non-audit services. (2) NOCLAR goes further, considering non-compliance causing substantial harm with serious financial or non-financial consequences. (3) SA 250 does not define stakeholders; NOCLAR is about investors, creditors, employees and the public. (4) Imminent-breach disclosure exists only under NOCLAR.
P.upd: Exam position: the SM scope above (the Nov 2026 RTP makes no change).

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: S.2(2) In practice / MCS
P.title: Section 2(2) — Members deemed to be in practice; Management Consultancy and other Services
P.short: Members deemed to be in practice; Management Consultancy and other Services
P.law: A member is deemed 'to be in practice' when, individually or in partnership with CAs in practice or members of prescribed professions, for remuneration received or to be received, he (i) engages in the practice of accountancy; (ii) offers to perform or performs auditing/verification of financial transactions, books, accounts or records, or preparation/verification/certification of financial accounting and related statements, or holds himself out to the public as an accountant; (iii) renders professional services or assistance on accounting procedure or recording, presentation or certification of financial facts or data; (iv) renders such other services as, in the Council's opinion, are or may be rendered by a CA in practice.
notes: Explanation: an ACA/FCA who is a salaried employee of a CA in practice or a CA firm is deemed to be in practice for the limited purpose of training articled assistants.
Offering alone is enough: setting up an establishment offering accounting services = in practice, even with no client. Service with armed forces = deemed in practice.

Regulation 191: acting in professional capacity (not personal/employee) as liquidator, trustee, executor, administrator, arbitrator, receiver, adviser or representative for costing, financial or taxation matters, or taking up an appointment by Central/State Government, court or legal authority, or acting as Secretary — unless on a salary-cum-full-time basis — is deemed practice.

MCS under s.2(2)(iv) excludes statutory/periodical audit, tax representation/advice, liquidator, trustee, executor, administrator, arbitrator, receiver. Includes (xxxii items in 2026 Code): financial management planning; capital structure and raising finance; working capital; project reports and feasibility studies (tax implications of (i)–(iv) count as MCS); cash budgets and cash flow; budgeting; inventory management; market research; price fixation; management accounting, cost control; control methods and MIS; personnel recruitment and selection; incentive plans; management and operational audits (2026: including Information System Audit); valuation of shares and business, M&A advice, Registered Valuer; business policy and corporate planning; organisation structure, HR development, training programmes; systems analysis and design, software, EDP; adviser/consultant to an issue (drafting prospectus, listing formalities, publicity budget, selection of agencies, post-issue activities); investment counselling in securities; registrar to an issue and share transfer; quality audit; environment audit; energy audit; recovery consultant in banking; insurance financial advisory including insurance brokerage (not agency); insolvency professional; administrative services; forensic accounting and investigation; research analyst recognised by a regulator; social impact/CSR impact/BRSR assessment; AI consultancy.
Explicitly not permitted: broking, underwriting and portfolio management.

Administrative services: routine/clerical, little or no judgment — word processing, preparing statutory forms for client approval, submitting them as instructed, monitoring filing dates; e.g., GST practitioner functions under Rule 83(8) CGST Rules.
Registered Valuer: CAs qualify for securities or financial assets only, not plant and machinery.

Correlate with s.144 Companies Act: auditor cannot render accounting and book-keeping, internal audit, design and implementation of financial information system, actuarial, investment advisory, investment banking, outsourced financial services, management services, to the company, its holding or subsidiary.
P.upd: Beyond the Nov 2026 syllabus (not in RTP): the 2026 Code MCS list adds forensic accounting and investigation, research analyst recognised by a regulator, social impact/CSR/BRSR assessment (from 11 Dec 2025) and AI consultancy, and item (xiv) includes Information System Audit.

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: S.6 COP
P.title: Section 6 — Certificate of Practice; Regulations 10 and 11
P.law: No member shall be entitled to practise, whether in India or elsewhere, unless he has obtained a certificate of practice from the Council. Annual fee payable on or before 1 April each year. COP may be cancelled in prescribed circumstances.
notes: A member not in practice cannot accept engagements of the type normally prescribed for a CA, even if no special qualification is needed for it.

Suspended member: cannot practise in any other capacity (e.g., as income-tax practitioner) during suspension — once a member, bound by the Act (A.C. Kaher case). A removed member cannot appear before tax authorities during removal.

Reg 10 — COP cancelled if: name removed from Register; COP obtained on incorrect/false information or by mistake (after hearing); member ceased to practise; annual COP fee not paid by 30 September of the relevant year.
Reg 11 — Restoration: where cancelled for non-payment, restored from date of cancellation if application and fee reach before expiry of the relevant year.
Practising without COP = contravention of the Act → SS II(1); representing to be in practice without COP → S.24–26 Penalties.

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: S.7 Designation
P.title: Section 7 — Use of designation 'Chartered Accountant'
P.law: Every member in practice shall, and any other member may, use the designation of a chartered accountant, and no member using it shall use any other description, in addition or in substitution. May add letters/description of membership of another recognised institute of accountancy or any other qualification he possesses. A firm, all of whose partners are members in practice, may be known as Chartered Accountants.
notes: Prefix 'CA' can be used by all members, in practice or not.

Not allowed on professional documents: Income-tax Consultant, Cost Accountant, Company Secretary, Cost Consultant, Management Consultant, Corporate Lawyer, CPA, positions like Director, MP, member of political party, club positions.

Allowed: A.C.M.A./F.C.M.A. letters (not 'Cost Accountant'); membership of foreign accountancy institutes recognised through MoU/MRA (e.g., SAICA, CPA Ireland, ICAEW); 'Insolvency Professional' and 'Registered Valuer' on visiting cards and letterheads; university degrees.
Practice as advocate/CS/CMA with permission: never use 'Chartered Accountant' simultaneously with those designations.

Category IV Merchant Banker/adviser to issue: name may appear in offer documents under 'Advisor/Consultant to the Issue', not prominently, never as 'Merchant Banker'; not to be used on own stationery.
ICFAI v. ICAI (SC, 2007): 'any other qualification' means qualification other than one granted by an institute of accountancy, subject to Council recognition.

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: S.8 Disabilities
P.title: Section 8 — Disabilities for membership
P.law: A person shall not be entitled to have his name entered in or borne on the Register if he: (i) has not attained 21 years at the time of application; (ii) is of unsound mind and so adjudged by a competent court; (iii) is an undischarged insolvent or undischarged bankrupt; (iiia) is declared bankrupt under the IBC, 2016; (iv) being a discharged insolvent, has not obtained a court certificate that insolvency was caused by misfortune without misconduct; (v) has been convicted by a court in or outside India of an offence involving moral turpitude and punishable with imprisonment, or of a non-technical offence committed in professional capacity, unless pardoned or the Central Government removes the disability; (vi) has been removed from membership on being found guilty of professional or other misconduct (for a specified period — until expiry).
notes: Failure to disclose a disability is itself professional misconduct; Council may remove the name.

Also note s.5 (Associates and Fellows): Fellow = associate in continuous practice in India for 5 years, or associate for 5 continuous years with prescribed equivalent qualifications. Acting as fellow without being one → FS III(1).
s.19 Register particulars: full name, date of birth, domicile, residential and professional address, date of entry, qualifications, whether COP held, others prescribed.
P.upd: Wording per 2022 amendment (w.e.f. 10 May 2022): 'Register of members', 'undischarged bankrupt', IBC bankruptcy, conviction 'in or outside India', 'transportation' deleted.

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: S.20 Removal
P.title: Section 20 — Removal of name from Register; restoration
P.short: Removal of name from Register; restoration
P.law: Council may remove the name of a member who (a) is dead; (b) requests so; (c) has not paid any prescribed fee; (d) was or has become subject to a s.8 disability or has otherwise ceased to be entitled. Council shall remove the name where an order removing him from membership has been passed under the Act.
notes: Removed for non-payment: may be re-entered on paying arrears of annual fee, entrance fee and additional fee (Reg 19).

Effective date of restoration: application and fees in the same year of removal → from date of removal; removal under orders of BoD/DC/Appellate Authority/High Court → as per such orders; other cases → from the date application and fee are received.

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: S.21 Disciplinary mechanism
P.title: Sections 21, 21A–21D, 22G — Disciplinary mechanism
P.law: Complaint (with fee) or information → Director (Discipline) forms a prima facie opinion → First Schedule matters to Board of Discipline (BoD); Second Schedule or both Schedules to Disciplinary Committee (DC).
notes: No prima facie case: placed before BoD; BoD may close if it agrees, or advise Director (Discipline) to investigate further.
BoD penalties (First Schedule): reprimand; removal from Register up to 3 months; fine up to ₹1,00,000.
DC penalties (Second Schedule/both): reprimand; removal permanently or for any period it thinks fit; fine up to ₹5,00,000.
Director (Discipline), BoD and DC have civil court powers: summoning and examining on oath, discovery and production of documents, evidence on affidavit.
Appeal (s.22G): member aggrieved, or Director (Discipline) with Council authorisation, may appeal to the Appellate Authority within 90 days of communication of the order.

Appellate Authority may: confirm, modify or set aside the order; impose, set aside, reduce or enhance the penalty; remit the case for further enquiry; pass such other order as it thinks fit — after giving parties a hearing.
Also see NFRA (s.132(4) Companies Act) for prescribed classes of companies — investigates misconduct, imposes penalty and debars (see case scenario Q-CS1).
P.mem: First → Board (3 months, 1 lakh). Second → Committee (permanent, 5 lakh). Appeal 90 days.

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: S.22 Misconduct defined
P.title: Section 22 — Professional or other misconduct defined; 'other misconduct'
P.short: Professional or other misconduct defined; 'other misconduct'
P.law: 'Professional or other misconduct' includes any act or omission in any of the Schedules, but nothing limits the power of the Director (Discipline) under s.21(1) to inquire into the conduct of any member under any other circumstances.
notes: Professional misconduct: FS Parts I, II, III and SS Parts I, II.
Other misconduct: FS Part IV and SS Part III — covers conduct even outside professional work (e.g., forging the will of a relative).
B. Mukherjea (SC, 1958): even conduct not attracting any clause of the Schedules can be inquired into if it renders the member unfit.
Schedule structure: FS Part I (12 clauses), II (2), III (3), IV (2); SS Part I (10), II (5), III (1).

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: S.24–26 Penalties
P.title: Sections 24, 25, 26 — Offences and penalties
P.law: s.24: a non-member representing himself as a member or using the designation CA, or a member without COP representing that he is in practice or practising as CA — first conviction fine up to ₹1 lakh; subsequent conviction imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹5 lakh, or both. s.25: no company (including an LLP having a company as partner) shall practise as chartered accountants; every director/manager/secretary/officer knowingly a party — fine ₹2 lakh to ₹10 lakh on first conviction, ₹4 lakh to ₹20 lakh subsequently. s.26: no person other than a member shall sign any document on behalf of a CA in practice or a CA firm in professional capacity — first conviction fine ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh; subsequent imprisonment up to 1 year or fine ₹2 lakh to ₹10 lakh, or both.
notes: An LLP without a company as partner can practise and take audits; s.141(2) Companies Act: only CA partners act and sign for the firm.
Prem Batra (1989): non-member held guilty under s.24(i)(a) and (b).
P.upd: Your SM shows the old amounts (s.24: ₹1,000 / ₹5,000; s.25: up to ₹1,000 / ₹5,000). The Act was amended in 2022 (in force 10 May 2022) and the figures above are current law, but the RTP does not mention them. In the exam quote the SM figures and, if you like, add that the 2022 amendment enhanced them.

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: S.27 Branch offices
P.title: Section 27 — Maintenance of branch offices
P.law: If a CA in practice or a CA firm has more than one office in India, each office shall be in the separate charge of a member of the Institute.
notes: Exemption (one member may be in charge of two offices): second office in the same premises, or in the same city, or within 50 km of the municipal limits of the city of the first office. Declare which is the main office (professional address).
Member in charge must be actively associated: resides at that place or attends that office for at least 182 days a year (or as the Executive Committee decides).
Member in charge of a branch must be a partner or a whole-time paid assistant.

Hill areas: temporary office in the plains for up to 3 months a year; regular office continues; name board only during the period; not on letterheads; intimate the Institute before each winter and on closure (by registered post).
Office = place where a name board is fixed or which is mentioned on letterhead/documents as place of business.
Name board at residence: only an individual name plate with designation CA, not the firm's name board.

P.g: B. CA Act, 1949 — key sections
P.label: KYC norms
P.title: KYC norms for CAs in practice (mandatory for attestation assignments)
P.short: KYC norms for CAs in practice (mandatory for attestation assignments)
P.law: Council-approved KYC norms are mandatory and apply to all assignments pertaining to attestation functions.
notes: Individual/proprietor: name; PAN or Aadhaar; business description; last audited FS; type of engagement.
Corporate entity: name and address; business description; parent company (if subsidiary); last audited FS; type of engagement; company PAN, CIN; directors' names, addresses and DINs.
Non-corporate entity: name and address; PAN; business description; partners' names and addresses with PAN/Aadhaar/DIN; last audited FS; type of engagement.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(1)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (1) — Allowing another to practise in his name
P.short: Allowing another to practise in his name
P.law: A CA in practice is guilty if he allows any person to practise in his name as a chartered accountant unless such person is also a chartered accountant in practice and is in partnership with or employed by him.
notes: Protects the public from unqualified persons practising under cover of a qualified CA. Allowed: CA-in-practice partner or employee. Not allowed: non-CA, or a CA who is neither partner nor employee.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(2)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (2) — Sharing fees/profits with non-members
P.law: Guilty if he pays or allows or agrees to pay or allow, directly or indirectly, any share, commission or brokerage in the fees or profits of his professional business, to any person other than a member of the Institute, a partner or retired partner, the legal representative of a deceased partner, a member of any other professional body, or such other persons having such qualifications as may be prescribed, for rendering such professional services from time to time in or outside India. Explanation: 'partner' includes a person residing outside India with whom a partnership not in contravention of item (4) exists.
notes: Reg 53A(1) professional bodies: ICSI, ICMAI (Cost), Bar Council of India, Indian Institute of Architects, Institute of Actuaries of India; also foreign accountancy bodies recognised under s.29(2).
Reg 53A(3) persons qualified in India (items 2, 3, 4, 5): CS, Cost Accountant, Actuary, B.E., B.Tech, B.Arch, LL.B from recognised universities, MBA from recognised universities/AICTE institutions.
Substance over form: 50% of audit fees paid to a non-CA as 'office allowance' for years = sharing of profits → guilty.
A percentage of audit fee deducted by Government (e.g., Registrar of Co-operative Societies) to meet administrative expenses — no bar.

Goodwill: widow/legal representative of a deceased partner may receive a share of profits only if the partnership deed so provides. For a proprietary firm, goodwill may be sold to an eligible member after the proprietor's death; consideration in instalments allowed but not contingent on future profits. Procedure: application by a COP holder; death certificate, draft sale deed, succession/legal heir documents; NOC of other legal heirs (spouse, children, parents); advertisement inviting objections; Form 18 within 30 days of approval. Same applies where all partners of a firm die together.
Monthly lump-sum or percentage of income to widow of deceased member for 5 years — not permissible (it is fee sharing, not goodwill).
P.upd: Exam position: 1 year (SM). ICAI's Ethical Standards Board later announced an increase to three years; it is not among the Nov 2026 RTP amendments.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(3)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (3) — Accepting profits of a non-member's work
P.short: Accepting profits of a non-member's work
P.law: Guilty if he accepts or agrees to accept any part of the profits of the professional work of a person who is not a member of the Institute. Proviso: profit sharing or similar arrangements, including receiving share, commission or brokerage in fees, with a member of a professional body or person with prescribed qualifications referred to in item (2) are allowed.
notes: Reason: a CA often recommends other professionals to clients; he must not earn from their fees.
Referral fees between members in practice are not prohibited.
Contrast with employee rule: a member in service accepting commission from a lawyer engaged by employer → FS II(2).

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(4)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (4) — Partnership with non-members
P.law: Guilty if he enters into partnership, in or outside India, with any person other than a CA in practice or such other person who is a member of any other professional body having prescribed qualifications, including a resident who but for his residence abroad would be entitled to be registered under s.4(1)(v), or whose qualifications are recognised by the Central Government or Council for this purpose.
notes: Reg 53B bodies for partnership: CS (ICSI), Cost Accountant (ICMAI), Advocate (Bar Council), Engineer (Institution of Engineers or engineering degree), Architect (IIA), Actuary (IAI); plus foreign accountancy bodies recognised under s.29(2). Multi-disciplinary partnerships per Council guidelines.
A CA in practice who is an Insolvency Professional or Registered Valuer may be a partner in an IPE/RVE registered with IBBI consisting of Reg 53B professionals (intimate the Institute).
A CA in practice cannot be partner/designated partner in an LLP not carrying out professional work (director simplicitor is a different case).
Prohibition is confined to the practice of the profession (Iqbal Hamid, Nalin S. Sualy).
No fresh partnerships with members of foreign bodies earlier permitted under s.4(1)(v) after 8 Dec 1997.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(5)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (5) — Securing work through non-employees or improper means
P.short: Securing work through non-employees or improper means
P.law: Guilty if he secures, either through the services of a person who is not an employee of such CA or who is not his partner or by means which are not open to a chartered accountant, any professional business. Proviso: arrangements permitted under items (2), (3) and (4) are allowed.
notes: 'A man must stand erect, and not be kept erect by others.' All canvassing is unethical.
Jethanand Sharda v. Deepak Mehta (1998): letters to Army Canteen officers with personal details and fee norms → guilty under (5) and (6).
Acts of partners and employees to secure work are themselves subject to clauses (6) and (7).

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(6)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (6) — Soliciting clients or professional work
P.law: Guilty if he solicits clients or professional work either directly or indirectly by circular, advertisement, personal communication or interview or by any other means. Provisos: nothing prevents (i) applying, requesting, inviting or securing work from another CA in practice; (ii) responding to tenders or enquiries issued by users of professional services and securing work as a consequence.
notes: Permitted announcements: changes in partnership, dissolution, change of address/phone — bare facts, appropriate area and number of insertions. Classified ad in ICAI Journal/Newsletter for sharing work, partnership or employment: name, address, phone, mobile, fax, e-mail, website, social media addresses, plus factual experience and specialisation relevant to the ad.

Empanelment: may write to a known panel-maintaining body (govt, PSU, courts, co-operatives, banks) to be empanelled; no roving enquiries; may quote fees on enquiry or respond to tenders from such bodies.
Tenders: see GL: Tenders. EMD reasonable; exorbitant EMD may be examined by ESB. Keep a cost sheet.
Books/articles/presentations: may state designation CA and firm name; no professional attainments.
Greeting cards/invitations: designation and firm name allowed on greetings, marriage/religious ceremony invitations, office opening, change of premises/phone — only to clients, relatives and friends.
Ads for Silver/Golden/Diamond/Platinum/Centenary celebrations of a firm allowed; other firm events not advertised.
Sponsorship: not allowed, except ICAI CPE events approved by Council/CPE Directorate. CSR activities: individual name with prefix 'CA' only, no firm name or CA logo.
Coaching/teaching: no hoardings, posters, banners advertising association; only a sign board outside premises with institute name, contact details and subjects.
Firm profile to a prospective client: only in response to the client's specific query.
TV/movie credits: name not displayed differently from other credits.
Roving letters/e-mails to persons likely to need a CA = advertisement → prohibited. Circulars seeking work from colleagues, except the ICAI-journal classified route, prohibited.

Representation under s.140(4) Companies Act: dignified; how he acted independently and conscientiously; may state willingness to be reappointed; no publicity or canvassing (e.g., no list of contributions to controls).
Client introduced by another member: do not accept its original work; ask client to come through the introducing member.
Public interviews: no publicity or highlighting attainments; facts only, in response to specific questions.
Box-number advertisements soliciting work: prohibited.
Educational videos: see 2026 update below.
Websites: see Adv: Website.
P.upd: Exam position (SM): educational videos may not refer to the member's firm and may not contain contact details or website address. The Code of Ethics 2026 relaxes this (firm name and contact details allowed, website still not), but that change is not in the Nov 2026 RTP.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(7)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (7) — Advertising attainments; other designations
P.law: Guilty if he advertises his professional attainments or services, or uses any designation or expressions other than chartered accountant on professional documents, visiting cards, letter heads or sign boards, unless it be a degree of a university established by law in India or recognised by the Central Government, or a title indicating membership of ICAI or of any other institution recognised by the Central Government or the Council. Proviso: a member in practice may advertise through a write-up setting out services and particulars of his firm, subject to Council guidelines.
notes: Write-up rules → Adv: Write-up.
Improper designations: see S.7 Designation. Also not 'Member of Parliament', 'Municipal Councillor' alongside CA.
Date of setting up practice/establishment of firm must not appear on letterheads and professional documents. (It may appear in a write-up and on a website — 'year of establishment'.)
Personal letterhead showing all firms in which the member is a partner: permitted.
Firm name with 'Chartered Accountants' only on professional documents, visiting cards, letterheads, sign boards; individuals may use prefix 'CA'.
Press notice of exam success: no undesirable publicity; name, address, school, prize/rank, principal's name, firm and town may appear.
Reports and certificates: publication limited to what serves their purpose; issue on firm letterhead.

Electronic media/lectures: may describe self as CA and give directly relevant special qualifications; firm name may be mentioned (per Code); no exaggerated claims or comparison; objective, not promotional. At talks/conferences: describe as CA only when acting as CA; no reference to the firm.
Training courses for staff may include staff of other CAs and clients; no undue prominence to the CA's name.
Sign board: discretion and good taste; illumination only for visibility; no glow signs/large lit boards like traders.

Director of a company: prospectus/public announcements must not describe the CA's expertise or attainments; 'Chartered Accountant' and other directorships allowed; firm name not. Ask the company to get such material approved by him.
Logo: members may use the common CA India logo (blue CA with tricolour inverted tick, 'India', white background; don't alter). Firm-specific logos/monograms prohibited on any display material.
Network firms may advertise to the extent the advertisement guidelines permit and use 'Network Firms' on stationery.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(8)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (8) — Communication with previous auditor
P.law: Guilty if he accepts a position as auditor previously held by another chartered accountant or a certified auditor under the Restricted Certificate Rules, 1932, without first communicating with him in writing.
notes: Purpose: not mere courtesy — to learn if there are professional reasons not to accept; protects the incoming auditor, the public and the outgoing auditor's independence. Clients may change auditors at will (subject to statute).

Professional reasons not to accept: (a) non-compliance of ss.139/140 (FS I(9)); (b) non-payment of undisputed audit fee (not for sick units) → GL: Unpaid undisputed fee; (c) qualified report by the previous auditor — may accept only if satisfied the previous auditor's qualification was not justified. First two → accepting is misconduct.
A fee dispute is not a valid professional reason to refuse; use influence to get it settled.

Positive evidence of delivery required: registered post A/D; hand delivery against written acknowledgement; acknowledgement via e-mail registered with ICAI or last known official e-mail; UDIN-based (per guidelines). Certificate of posting is not enough (J.S. Bhati v. ICAI, Rajasthan HC).
Returned 'office found locked' = deemed delivered. 'No such office' at ICAI-registered address = deemed delivered unless the retiring auditor proves otherwise.
No reply after reasonable time → may proceed.

Applies to all audits: statutory, tax, GST, internal, concurrent or any other audit. For non-CA previous auditors, healthy practice to communicate. Special audit under Income-tax Act: healthy to communicate with statutory auditor.
Government/bank audits with no time: send the communication, give conditional acceptance subject to professional objections, start urgent work, decide finally after the reply.
Undisputed fee unpaid and previous auditor unavailable: client may buy a DD for the amount; incoming auditor verifies and may accept, ensuring payment reaches the predecessor.
Must communicate before accepting — writing after starting work does not cure the breach.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(9)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (9) — Ascertaining compliance with ss.139–141
P.law: Guilty if he accepts an appointment as auditor of a company without first ascertaining from it whether the requirements of s.225 of the Companies Act, 1956 (ss.139 to 141 of the Companies Act, 2013) or any other law pertaining to appointment of auditors have been duly complied with.
notes: Nov 2026 RTP amendment: wording now reads 'section 225 of the Companies Act, 1956, or sections 139 to 141 of the Companies Act, 2013 or any other law pertaining to appointment of auditors for the time being in force'.
'Ascertain' = find out for certain: verify records, a management certificate is not enough. If the company refuses access, do not accept.
First auditor: Board resolution within 30 days of registration (or general meeting properly convened if Board failed).
Casual vacancy: Board has power and passed resolution; if due to resignation, general meeting approval.
Removal before term: special resolution and prior Central Government approval.

Replacing retiring auditor (s.140(4)): special notice by a member (not earlier than 3 months, at least 14 days before meeting); sent to members at least 7 days before the meeting (s.115); copy sent forthwith to retiring auditor (preferably registered A/D — certificate of posting not adequate); retiring auditor's representation circulated and considered; resolution validly passed. Obtain true copy of the notice and certified minutes.
s.139(10): if no auditor is appointed or reappointed at the AGM, the existing auditor continues. A person declining the AGM appointment does not create a casual vacancy for the Board to fill.
Adjourned AGM: retiring auditor continues till the adjourned meeting concludes; special notice received after adjournment cannot be acted upon.
Then also comply with FS I(8).

Unjustified removal: ESB reviews. Resigning/not re-offering auditor with professional reasons communicates to the Board with copy to ICAI; auditor not reappointed files his statement with ICAI; the incoming auditor must obtain and consider these before accepting. Follow Council direction not to accept → GL: Unjustified removal.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(10)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (10) — Percentage/contingent fees; Regulation 192
P.law: Guilty if he charges or offers to charge, accepts or offers to accept in respect of any professional employment, fees which are based on a percentage of profits or which are contingent upon the findings, or results of such employment, except as permitted under any regulation made under the Act.
notes: Fees fixed by a court or public authority are not 'contingent'.

Regulation 192 exceptions: (a) receiver/liquidator — % of realisation or disbursement of assets; (b) auditor of a co-operative society — % of paid-up capital, working capital, gross/net income or profits; (c) valuer for direct taxes and duties — % of value of property valued; (d) certain management consultancy services decided by Council — % basis/contingent; (e) fund raising — % of funds raised; (f) debt recovery — % of debt recovered; (g) cost optimisation — % of benefit derived; (h) other services decided by Council: acting as Insolvency Professional; non-assurance services to non-audit clients.
So a contingent fee for tax appeal work is fine for a non-audit client only.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(11)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (11) — Other business or occupation; Regs 190A, 191
P.law: Guilty if he engages in any business or occupation other than the profession of chartered accountant unless permitted by the Council. Proviso: may be a director of a company (not managing or whole-time director) unless he or any of his partners is interested in such company as an auditor.
notes: Reg 190A: no other business except with Council permission. Reg 191: may act as liquidator, trustee, executor, administrator, arbitrator, receiver, adviser/representative for costing/financial/taxation, government/court appointment or Secretary in professional capacity, if not salary-cum-full-time.

General permission (no specific approval): employment under CAs in practice; private tutorship; authorship of books/articles; LIC agency for renewal commission only; attending classes/exams; public elective office (MP, MLA, MLC); honorary office in charitable/educational/non-commercial bodies; Notary Public, Justice of Peace, Special Executive Magistrate; part-time tutorship under ICAI coaching; paper valuation, paper-setter, head examiner, moderator; editorship of professional journals; surveyor and loss assessor under Insurance Act; recovery consultant in banking; owning agricultural land and agriculture.

Specific prior permission: employment in business concerns where member/relatives don't hold substantial interest; employment in non-business concerns; MD/WTD of a body corporate (no substantial interest); interest in family business (inherited, not actively managed); interest in an educational institution; lectureship for courses other than ICAI's; tutorship under an educational institution other than ICAI coaching; editorship of non-professional journals; any other the Executive Committee allows.
Permission must be taken before engaging — applying afterwards does not cure the gap.

Relative (for these purposes): husband, wife, brother, sister, lineal ascendant or descendant. Substantial interest: company — ≥20% voting power (non-fixed-dividend shares) held by member and/or relatives and their concerns; other concern — entitled to ≥20% of profits.
s.2(54) Companies Act: a person entrusted with substantially the whole management can be a deemed MD/WTD.

Director simplicitor: generally permitted in any company unless he or any partner is its auditor. ESB: auditor of a subsidiary cannot be director of its holding company. Promoter/subscriber and director simplicitor: allowed.
Corporate form: MD/WTD/Manager of a company exclusively rendering MCS and registered with ICAI — permitted, retains full-time COP → GL: Corporate form (MCS co.).
HUF/family business: inherited interest, not actively engaged, not created by him; declaration to decentralised office. Karta investing HUF funds only, not actively managing — within limits.

ESB decisions: equity research adviser allowed, but publishing a retail research report = other business. Equity and currency derivatives in personal capacity allowed; commodity derivatives not allowed; derivatives for clients not allowed.
Teaching hours: general and specific permission for tutorship subject to direct teaching hours not exceeding a weekly cap so that attest functions can be done.
P.upd: Exam position: 25 hours a week (SM). The Code of Ethics 2026 text states 35 hours, but the Nov 2026 RTP does not include this change.

P.g: C. First Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: FS I(12)
P.title: First Schedule, Part I, Clause (12) — Allowing others to sign
P.law: Guilty if he allows a person not being a member of the Institute in practice, or a member not being his partner, to sign on his behalf or on behalf of his firm, any balance sheet, profit and loss account, report or financial statements.
notes: Read with s.26 (S.24–26 Penalties).
'Report' = report from a professional assignment expressing a professional opinion (financial or non-financial). Includes certificates such as stock or GST production certificates.

May be delegated (no opinion involved): audit queries; asking for information/questionnaires; letters forwarding draft observations/FS; initialling and stamping vouchers and schedules; routine correspondence; memorandum of cash/physical verification; acknowledgements for records; bills and money receipts; routine tax matters subject to s.288 Income-tax Act; other office administration.
Delegation doesn't give a defence in a misconduct enquiry.
Where statute requires the signing member's name, disclose it; SA 700 requires membership number and FRN; generate UDIN → GL: UDIN.
Power of attorney to an employee CA to sign reports → guilty under this clause and SS Part II(1) for breach of s.26.

P.g: D. First Schedule — Parts II, III, IV
P.label: FS II(1)
P.title: First Schedule, Part II, Clause (1) — Member in service sharing emoluments
P.law: A member (other than in practice), being an employee of any company, firm or person, is guilty if he pays or allows or agrees to pay directly or indirectly to any person any share in the emoluments of the employment undertaken by him.
notes: Sharing with relatives/dependants/friends is not caught if unconnected with procuring or retaining the job. The job must be obtained and kept on merit.

P.g: D. First Schedule — Parts II, III, IV
P.label: FS II(2)
P.title: First Schedule, Part II, Clause (2) — Member in service accepting commission
P.law: Guilty if, being an employee, he accepts or agrees to accept any part of fees, profits or gains from a lawyer, a chartered accountant or broker engaged by such company, firm or person, or agent or customer of such company, firm or person, by way of commission or gratification.
notes: Applies whether whole-time or part-time employment, and even if he also holds COP.

P.g: D. First Schedule — Parts II, III, IV
P.label: FS III(1)
P.title: First Schedule, Part III, Clause (1) — Acting as a fellow
P.law: A member, whether in practice or not, is guilty if he, not being a fellow of the Institute, acts as a fellow.

P.g: D. First Schedule — Parts II, III, IV
P.label: FS III(2)
P.title: First Schedule, Part III, Clause (2) — Not supplying information to the Institute
P.short: Not supplying information to the Institute
P.law: Guilty if he does not supply the information called for, or does not comply with the requirements asked for, by the Institute, Council or any of its Committees, Director (Discipline), Board of Discipline, Disciplinary Committee, Quality Review Board or the Appellate Authority.
notes: Examples: not replying to ICAI letters on date of leaving/joining service; not disclosing other occupation in COP application; continuing to train an articled assistant after removal and not replying.
Contrast: giving false particulars to the Institute → SS II(3) (Second Schedule).

P.g: D. First Schedule — Parts II, III, IV
P.label: FS III(3)
P.title: First Schedule, Part III, Clause (3) — False information while seeking work
P.law: Guilty if, while inviting professional work from another CA or while responding to tenders or enquiries or while advertising through a write-up, or anything provided for in items (6) and (7) of Part I, he gives information knowing it to be false.

P.g: D. First Schedule — Parts II, III, IV
P.label: FS IV(1)
P.title: First Schedule, Part IV, Clause (1) — Conviction ≤ 6 months (other misconduct)
P.law: A member is guilty of other misconduct if he is held guilty by any civil or criminal court for an offence which is punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months.
notes: Punishable with more than 6 months → SS III(1) (Second Schedule, goes to DC).

P.g: D. First Schedule — Parts II, III, IV
P.label: FS IV(2)
P.title: First Schedule, Part IV, Clause (2) — Bringing disrepute
P.law: Guilty of other misconduct if, in the opinion of the Council, he brings disrepute to the profession or the Institute as a result of his action whether or not related to his professional work.
notes: E.g., concurrent auditor using influence to get a loan from the bank and defaulting.

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(1)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (1) — Disclosing client information
P.law: Guilty if he discloses information acquired in the course of his professional engagement to any person other than his client so engaging him, without the consent of his client or otherwise than as required by any law for the time being in force.
notes: Duty continues after the engagement ends.
Disclosure required to perform the service the client asked for (e.g., submissions to exchange control authorities) = implied consent; the initiative must come from the client.
Who gives consent: proprietor or his constituted attorney; any partner of a firm; for a company, the Board by resolution (s.179), or MD if Board powers are delegated comprehensively enough.

Working papers are the auditor's property; no duty to give access to the client or other auditors (including parent/subsidiary auditors, principal auditor vis-à-vis branch auditor, internal auditor). May, at discretion, give extracts to the client. Principal auditor may seek clarifications or visit the branch.
Information vs working papers: information may be given to the client or a regulator with client consent.
Legal compulsion where privilege (s.126 Evidence Act) can't be claimed: disclosure not misconduct; take legal advice.
s.143(12) Companies Act: fraud by officers/employees against the company must be reported to the Central Government as prescribed — a legal requirement, so not a breach.
Using client information at seminars/presentations without consent = breach, even for good intentions.

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(2)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (2) — Certifying without examination
P.law: Guilty if he certifies or submits in his name, or in the name of his firm, a report of an examination of financial statements unless the examination of such statements and the related records has been made by him or by a partner or an employee in his firm or by another chartered accountant in practice.
notes: Allows joint audits and use of another CA in practice.

SA 299 joint audit: divide work by units/areas/items/period; document and communicate division to the auditee; each joint auditor responsible for work allocated to him; jointly and severally responsible for work not divided, decisions about matters requiring joint judgment, examining that FS comply with statute, and ensuring the report complies with law. Each decides his own sampling and procedures. Management representations are a joint responsibility unless split by agreement.

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(3)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (3) — Vouching for forecasts
P.law: Guilty if he permits his name or the name of his firm to be used in connection with an estimate of earnings contingent upon future transactions in a manner which may lead to the belief that he vouches for the accuracy of the forecast.
notes: May prepare or review forecasts and projections if the report states sources of information, basis and major assumptions, and does not vouch for accuracy (Council, 1982). Same for hypothetical projections. See Guidance Note on Reports in Company Prospectuses (Revised 2019).
Issuing 97 projection statements without verifying basic documents, on which a bank lent → guilty under SS I (3), (7), (8).

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(4)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (4) — Opinion where substantial interest
P.law: Guilty if he expresses his opinion on financial statements of any business or enterprise in which he, his firm, or a partner in his firm has a substantial interest.
notes: 'Substantial interest' as in Appendix 9 of CA Regulations (20% test) → FS I(11). 'Financial statements' covers reports and certificates after examination under any statute or for tax; not statements prepared by employees for internal use.
Public conscience ahead of law: interpret independence strictly; avoid conflict of interest and duty (e.g., liquidator must not audit his own statement of accounts).

Council decisions: a CA in employment (even with COP) can't certify FS of his employer or a concern under the same management (unless law permits); can't audit a college where he is a part-time lecturer; can't audit a trust where his partner is an employee or trustee.
Applies to all attest functions — tax audit, GST audit, concurrent audits, borrower audits, stock exchange/broker audits.
Non-corporate entity: member owner/partner → shall not audit; partner or relative with substantial interest → should desist.

Companies (s.141(3)): officer/employee (b); partner or employee of an officer/employee (c); person, relative or partner holding security or interest in company, subsidiary, holding, associate or fellow subsidiary — relative may hold up to ₹1 lakh face value (d)(i); indebted beyond ₹5 lakh (d)(ii); guarantee/security for third party beyond ₹1 lakh (d)(iii); business relationship (e); relative is director or KMP (f). Director simplicitor can't audit that company (Council).
Certification for a relative (AS 18 definition) not permissible.

Council prohibitions: write books of account of audit clients; statutory auditor as internal auditor of the same entity; internal auditor as tax auditor; internal auditor as GST auditor; audit of a company within 2 years of completing tenure or resigning as its director.

Satisfy that appointment accords with the entity's statute/trust deed; regulator authorisation where needed (co-operatives, trusts); resolution of managing committee/trustees; engagement letter from firms/proprietors. s.288 Income-tax Act lists tax audit disqualifications.

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(5)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (5) — Failing to disclose a material fact
P.short: Failing to disclose a material fact
P.law: Guilty if he fails to disclose a material fact known to him which is not disclosed in a financial statement, but disclosure of which is necessary in making such financial statement where he is concerned with that financial statement in a professional capacity.
notes: Materiality must be established (SA 320); judge it for both balance sheet and P&L.

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(6)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (6) — Failing to report a known material misstatement
P.short: Failing to report a known material misstatement
P.law: Guilty if he fails to report a material misstatement known to him to appear in a financial statement with which he is concerned in a professional capacity.
notes: Materiality again the test. An authorised representative who only submits client-prepared statements on instructions is not 'reporting' on them (SM Illustration 31).

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(7)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (7) — Lack of due diligence / gross negligence
P.short: Lack of due diligence / gross negligence
P.law: Guilty if he does not exercise due diligence, or is grossly negligent in the conduct of his professional duties.
notes: Karnataka HC (1977): reasonable skill, care and caution; 'watchdog, not a bloodhound'; probe anything that excites suspicion.
Minor errors may not be gross negligence; Council may still flag them.

Examples: certifying circulation figures from MIS without books; not completing audit in time for statutory compliance; digitally signing ROC forms with a forged resignation letter without verification; certificates silent on basis and limitations misleading a bank.
A certificate is a written confirmation of facts; state limitations/assumptions and the documents relied on.

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(8)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (8) — Insufficient information for opinion
P.law: Guilty if he fails to obtain sufficient information which is necessary for expression of an opinion or its exceptions are sufficiently material to negate the expression of an opinion.
notes: Where limitation is so material, disclaim clearly (SA 705) — don't write 'subject to verification of the only asset, true and fair'.
Registrar of Newspapers v. K. Rajinder Singh (1971): circulation certificate without looking at financial records, bank statements, printer's bills → guilty.
Often charged together with (7) and (9) (NFRA case scenario).

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(9)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (9) — Material departure from generally accepted audit procedure
P.short: Material departure from generally accepted audit procedure
P.law: Guilty if he fails to invite attention to any material departure from the generally accepted procedure of audit applicable to the circumstances.
notes: GAAP-of-audit guidance: Engagement and Quality Control Standards, Statements, General Clarifications, Guidance Notes, Technical Guides, Practice Manuals.
A qualification does not excuse non-performance of a statutory duty (e.g., not verifying cash when it was necessary, feasible and material).
State reasons for inability to follow the procedure.
Listed company statutory audits only by peer-reviewed auditors with a valid certificate (SEBI).
Mention membership number and FRN on all attest reports; UDIN mandatory → GL: UDIN.
Special procedures: ABC circulation certification rules; bank verification rules.

P.g: E. Second Schedule — Part I (members in practice)
P.label: SS I(10)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (10) — Client money
P.law: Guilty if he fails to keep moneys of his client other than fees or remuneration or money meant to be expended in a separate banking account or to use such moneys for purposes for which they are intended within a reasonable time.
notes: Advance against services: outside this clause.
Money for expenses spent within a reasonably short time (statutory fees, stamp paper): no separate account needed.
Money for expenses not spent within a reasonably short time: separate account immediately.
Money received as trustee, executor, liquidator etc.: separate account immediately.

P.g: F. Second Schedule — Parts II, III
P.label: SS II(1)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part II, Clause (1) — Contravening the Act, Regulations or Council Guidelines
P.short: Contravening the Act, Regulations or Council Guidelines
P.law: A member, whether in practice or not, is guilty if he contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or the regulations made thereunder or any guidelines issued by the Council.
notes: The gateway for all Council Guidelines (GL: Books of account, GL: Tax audit limit, GL: Company audit limit, GL: Non-audit fee ceiling, GL: Indebtedness, GL: Unpaid undisputed fee, GL: UDIN etc.) and for breaches of sections like 6, 26, 27.
Regulations commonly breached: 43, 46, 47 (premium from articles), 48 (stipend), 56, 65, 67, 68–80 (audit assistants), 190 (register of offices/firms), 190A, 191, 192.
Peer Review Guidelines, 2022 are covered here too — compliance is obligatory.

P.g: F. Second Schedule — Parts II, III
P.label: SS II(2)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part II, Clause (2) — Employee disclosing confidential information
P.law: Guilty if he, being an employee of any company, firm or person, discloses confidential information acquired in the course of his employment except as and when required by any law for the time being in force or except as permitted by the employer.
notes: Applies to whole-time or part-time employment, even with COP. Law of agency principle.

P.g: F. Second Schedule — Parts II, III
P.label: SS II(3)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part II, Clause (3) — False particulars to the Institute
P.law: Guilty if he includes in any information, statement, return or form to be submitted to the Institute, Council or any of its Committees, Director (Discipline), Board of Discipline, Disciplinary Committee, Quality Review Board or the Appellate Authority any particulars knowing them to be false.
notes: J.R. Chatrath (1952): manager falsely claimed to be a partner in a fellowship application. K.S. Dugar (1987): false statement on oath before DC.
P.upd: Your SM lists A. Umanath Rao (1965) — not replying to ICAI letters — under this clause. For exam answers on 'failure to reply', the SM's own Illustration 27 and TYK 35 use First Schedule Part III(2) FS III(2); use that.

P.g: F. Second Schedule — Parts II, III
P.label: SS II(4)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part II, Clause (4) — Defalcation/embezzlement
P.law: Guilty if he defalcates or embezzles moneys received in his professional capacity.

P.g: F. Second Schedule — Parts II, III
P.label: SS II(5)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part II, Clause (5) — Acting as auditor in contravention of the Companies Act
P.short: Acting as auditor in contravention of the Companies Act
P.law: Guilty if he acts as an auditor of a company in contravention of the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.
notes: Inserted by the 2022 amendment; listed as a Nov 2026 amendment in the RTP (SM p.19.109). Use it with s.141 (disqualifications), s.139 (rotation, limits), s.144 (prohibited services).

P.g: F. Second Schedule — Parts II, III
P.label: SS III(1)
P.title: Second Schedule, Part III — Conviction > 6 months (other misconduct)
P.law: A member, whether in practice or not, is guilty of other misconduct if he is held guilty by any civil or criminal court for an offence which is punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding six months.
notes: Heard by the Disciplinary Committee. ≤ 6 months → FS IV(1).

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Books of account
P.title: Maintenance of books of account (Council General Guidelines 2008, Ch V)
P.short: Maintenance of books of account (Council General Guidelines 2008, Ch V)
P.law: A member in practice, or the firm in which he is a partner, shall maintain proper books of account for the professional practice, including a Cash Book and a Ledger.
notes: Applies irrespective of s.44AA Income-tax limits. Notes on a mobile phone are not books of account.

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Tax audit limit
P.title: Tax audit assignments under s.44AB — specified number (60)
P.law: As amended (Nov 2026 RTP): (i) the limit of 60 tax audit assignments per member is retained, reckoned per financial year; (ii) it is an aggregate limit for all tax audits accepted and signed by a member, individually and as partner of any firm(s) — an individual member cannot sign more than 60 tax audit reports in a financial year; (iii) the limit per partner cannot be distributed or shared between partners; (iv) it does not apply to tax audits under s.44AB(c), (d), (e) for persons covered by ss.44AE, 44ADA and 44AD; (v) a revised tax audit report is not counted.
notes: Partner of several firms: 60 in aggregate across all firms and individual capacity.
Old SM position (replaced): firm limit of 60 × partners could be distributed among partners in any manner (e.g., 6 partners → 360, one partner signing all). Pooling is no longer allowed.
Each year's audit is a separate assignment; head office and branches = one; one or more branches of the same concern by one CA = one.
Part-time practising partner not counted.
Audits under ss.44AD, 44ADA and 44AE were excluded from the count (SM).
Maintain a record of tax audits accepted in the prescribed format.
P.upd: Nov 2026 RTP (Chapter 19 amendment 3) replaces SM Chapter VI with the rule above. Its MCQ 1 (CA Chetan, 68 reports in a 4-partner firm) holds him guilty because the 60 applies to each member individually. SM Illustration 37's answer no longer holds.

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Unpaid undisputed fee
P.title: Appointment where undisputed audit fee of predecessor is unpaid (Ch VII)
P.short: Appointment where undisputed audit fee of predecessor is unpaid (Ch VII)
P.law: A member in practice shall not accept appointment as auditor of an entity if the undisputed audit fee of another CA for statutory audit under the Companies Act or other statutes has not been paid. Not applicable to a sick unit.
notes: Undisputed audit fee: provision for audit fee in accounts signed by both auditee and auditor, plus other expenses incurred by the auditor for the audit.
Sick unit: registered for at least 5 years, with accumulated losses at the end of any financial year equal to or exceeding its entire net worth.
Applies to statutory audit fees; the SM's Illustration 38 uses an unpaid tax audit fee and decides on the sick-unit exception — note both angles.

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Company audit limit
P.title: Specified number of company audits (Ch VIII)
P.short: Specified number of company audits (Ch VIII)
P.law: A member in practice shall not hold at any time more than the specified number of audit assignments of companies under s.141 Companies Act. SM: 30 per member/proprietary firm; for firms 30 per partner, including private companies, excluding One Person Companies and dormant companies.
notes: Partner in several firms/individual capacity: aggregate limit.
Count audits accepted singly or jointly with another CA/firm.
Head office and branches of a company = one; one or more branches of the same company = one.
Number of partners on the date of acceptance counts; a CA in full-time/part-time employment elsewhere and part-time practising partners are not counted.
Maintain a record in the prescribed format.
Compare s.141(3)(g) Companies Act: 20 company audits per person/partner, excluding OPCs, small companies, dormant companies and private companies with paid-up capital below ₹100 crore.
P.upd: Exam position: 30. The Code of Ethics 2026 raises the ceiling to 40, but the Nov 2026 RTP does not list it among the Chapter 19 amendments, so it is outside your exam cut-off. Write 30; you may add one line that the revised Code (effective 1 April 2026) raises it to 40.

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Non-audit fee ceiling
P.title: Appointment as statutory auditor — non-audit fee ceiling (Ch IX)
P.law: A member in practice shall not accept appointment as statutory auditor of PSUs, Government companies, listed companies and other public companies with turnover of ₹50 crore or more in a year, if he accepts other work/assignment/service for the same undertaking on remuneration which in total exceeds the fee for the statutory audit. Stricter conditions by the appointing authority/regulator prevail.
notes: Limit applies to the statutory auditor and his associate concerns together.

'Other work' includes MCS and all services permitted under s.2(2)(iv); excludes (a) audit under any other statute, (b) certification work required to be done by the statutory auditor, (c) any representation before an authority.

Associate concern: corporate body or partnership rendering MCS/permitted services where the auditor's proprietor/partners and/or relatives are directors/partners or together hold substantial interest.
Network: statutory auditor firm (with associates/common-partner firms) — same limit; other firms of the same network collectively — 3 times the statutory audit fee.
P.upd: Exam position: ₹50 crore (SM; no change in the Nov 2026 RTP).

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Indebtedness
P.title: Appointment when indebted to a concern (Ch X)
P.short: Appointment when indebted to a concern (Ch X)
P.law: A member in practice, a partner, a firm, or a relative of such member/partner shall not accept appointment as auditor of a concern while indebted to the concern, or having given any guarantee or security in connection with a third person's indebtedness to the concern, for limits fixed in the statute, and in other cases for amounts exceeding ₹1,00,000.
notes: Companies: statute limits — indebtedness above ₹5 lakh (s.141(3)(d)(ii)), guarantee/security above ₹1 lakh (s.141(3)(d)(iii)).
Fees recovered on a progressive basis as work is done (per terms of engagement) — auditor is not 'indebted' (Research Committee opinion).
P.upd: Exam position: ₹1,00,000 (SM; no change in the Nov 2026 RTP).

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Unjustified removal
P.title: Directions on unjustified removal of auditors (Ch XI)
P.short: Directions on unjustified removal of auditors (Ch XI)
P.law: An incoming auditor shall follow a direction of the Council or an appropriate Committee not to accept the appointment where the earlier auditor was removed unjustifiably.
notes: Procedure via Ethical Standards Board (statement of reasons filed with ICAI; incoming auditor obtains and considers it) — see FS I(9). ESB also has a prescribed form for complaint/statement of reasons for unjustified removal.

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Tenders
P.title: Guidelines on tenders (Ch XIII, Council Guideline dated 7 April 2016)
P.short: Guidelines on tenders (Ch XIII, Council Guideline dated 7 April 2016)
P.law: A member in practice shall not respond to any tender issued by an organisation or user of professional services in areas exclusively reserved for chartered accountants, such as audit and attestation. The restriction does not apply where the minimum fee is prescribed in the tender document itself, or where the areas are open to other professionals along with CAs.
notes: Minimum fee must commensurate with size, value, volume, manpower and nature of work; quoted fee not below that minimum.
Tenders issued on or after 7 April 2016 are covered.

May respond: tenders open to others (even if only CAs are invited); quotations called by individual letters; technical-bid-only tenders followed by financial quotes from shortlisted firms through individual letters.
EMD: reasonable amounts fine; exorbitant EMD may be examined by ESB. Keep a cost sheet (persons, hours) for ICAI's perusal. Institute may call for bid documents.
GeM portal: registration by CA firms permitted (operated by the client itself; not an aggregator or empanelment); follow tender guidelines when bidding.

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: UDIN
P.title: Unique Document Identification Number (Ch XIV)
P.law: A member in practice shall generate UDIN for all certificates (from 1 Feb 2019), GST and tax audit reports (from 1 Apr 2019) and all other audit, assurance and attestation functions (from 1 Jul 2019).
notes: Purpose: curb false certification by unauthorised persons, protect regulators and banks. UDIN also recognised as evidence of communication with previous auditor under FS I(8).

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Networking
P.title: Guidelines for networking (Ch XV)
P.law: A larger structure aimed at co-operation is a network if it shares any of: profit or cost sharing; common ownership, control or management; common quality control policies; common business strategy; common brand name; significant professional resources.
notes: Not a network by itself: mere referral arrangement; sharing immaterial costs; sharing only audit methodology/manual/training development costs; joint bid for a single proposal; association with an unrelated entity to jointly provide a service.
Judgment: reasonable and informed third party test; apply consistently.
Referencing membership of an association on stationery may create the appearance of a network.
Forms: mutual entity (facilitator, no practice), partnership (up to 20 partners), LLP, company (per corporate form guidelines). Constituents: sole proprietors, partnerships, other permitted entities.
A firm may join only one network; firms with common partners join only one network.

Name: approved by ICAI; use '& Affiliates', never '& Co.' or '& Associates' (e.g., AB & Affiliates; AB Affiliates LLP; AB Affiliates P. Ltd). Form A; ICAI decides within 30 days. Name approval alone doesn't allow practice in that name.

Registration: Form B within 3 months of name approval (name reserved 3 months); mandatory. Indian firms networked with a common multinational firm are a network. Network with entities outside India: Form D within 30 days. Change in constitution: Form C within 30 days.

Ethics: if one network firm is statutory auditor, others shall not take internal audit, book-keeping or other assignments prohibited for the auditor; non-audit fee ceiling as in GL: Non-audit fee ceiling (other network firms collectively 3×); where rotation is prescribed, a network firm cannot replace a retiring firm of the same network; advertising per guidelines; 'Network Firms' on stationery.
Registration with ICAI = public notice, so client consent deemed obtained.

Bye-laws cover managing committee, administration, fees, engagement partner, dispute resolution, training, newsletters, software, databases, library, technical director, resources and compensation, peer review.
P.upd: Beyond the Nov 2026 syllabus (not in RTP): under the 2026 Code, network firms registered with ICAI may create their own websites.

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Corporate form (MCS co.)
P.title: Corporate form of practice — Management Consultancy Company (Ch XVII)
P.law: Members in practice may be MD, WTD or Manager of a body corporate engaged exclusively in Management Consultancy and Other Services permitted under s.2(2)(iv), subject to Council conditions, and retain full-time COP.
notes: No restriction on equity holding (self and relatives). Treated as full-time practice: can do attest functions individually or in a firm and train articled/audit assistants.
Company name approved by and company registered with ICAI (from 1 Oct 2006). No audit practice in corporate form.

Ethics: if the individual/firm is statutory auditor, the MCS company shall not take internal audit, book-keeping or other prohibited assignments; non-audit fee ceiling applies; comply with FS I (6) and (7) and give an undertaking; render only MCS.

P.g: G. Council Guidelines (Guidelines on Ethical Issues)
P.label: GL: Logo
P.title: Logo guidelines (Ch XVI)
P.law: Members may use the CA India logo as published (blue 'CA', tricolour inverted tick, 'India', white background). No alteration of font, colour, spacing, proportion; no rotation or distortion. Firm logos/monograms of any kind are prohibited.
notes: One-year transition was allowed for replacing old stationery and signage.

P.g: H. Advertisement, write-up and website
P.label: Adv: Write-up
P.title: Advertisement through write-up (Council Guidelines for Advertisement, 2008)
P.short: Advertisement through write-up (Council Guidelines for Advertisement, 2008)
P.law: Members may advertise through a write-up setting out their or their firm's particulars and services, maintaining the profession's dignity. ICAI does not pre-approve write-ups and may direct removal.
notes: Conditions: (A) honest and truthful; (B) no exaggerated claims about services, qualifications or experience; (C) no disparaging references or unsubstantiated comparisons; (D) not bring disrepute; (E) no testimonials/endorsements, no client names (past or present), no fees charged; (F) no achievements/awards (except Central/State Government or regulator awards), positions held or accreditations; (G) no monogram or catch words; (H) membership number/FRN mandatory; (I) font size not exceeding 14; (J) not violate the Act, Regulations, Code or Council guidelines.

Member write-up may contain: name with CA; membership no.; age; dates of ACA/FCA; date from which COP held; recognised qualifications; languages; phone/mobile/fax; professional address; website; e-mail; CA logo; passport-style photo; number of employees (CAs, other professionals, articles/audit assistants, others) and their particulars; services provided; position as Director/MD in an ICAI-registered MCS company.

Firm write-up may contain: firm name with 'Chartered Accountants'; FRN; year of establishment; registered addresses (HO and branches); working hours; phones; e-mail; number of partners; partners' particulars and photos; CA logo; employee details; services provided; affiliation with an ICAI-registered network. May be signed with name, place and date.

Directories: telephone/trade directories — only under 'Chartered Accountants', only for the member's own town, alphabetical, not differential/prominent, open to all CAs of that town; trade/social directories allowed. App-based aggregators listing other trades — not allowed. Third-party advisory websites: consultancy/advice only, no contact address, no attainments, just the statement of being CA; firm name with 'Chartered Accountants' not allowed. Specialised directories/'Who's Who': name, description, address, directorships, personal details, outside interests — no client names.

Exemptions (press ads with name and 'Chartered Accountants', not more prominent than usual): recruiting staff for own office; on behalf of clients needing staff or buying/selling business/property; sale of business/property as trustee, liquidator or receiver. Avoid 'a well-known firm' in staff ads.
P.upd: Exam position: the SM conditions above, including membership no./FRN and font size 14. The Code of Ethics 2026 liberalises write-ups, but that is not in the Nov 2026 RTP.

P.g: H. Advertisement, write-up and website
P.label: Adv: Website
P.title: Website of CA firms (pull model) and social media
P.short: Website of CA firms (pull model) and social media
P.law: Members and firms may create their own websites in any format, subject to conditions; websites run on a 'pull' model, not 'push': information reaches a person only on a specific pull request.
notes: Don't circulate website information by e-mail or any other mode except on a specific pull request; don't issue circulars or ads soliciting visits. Website address may appear on professional stationery and e-mail.
